name: Mercy Itunuoluwa Olalere
missingPieces: Capstone D2 omitted Artefact 04 and gave an incorrect final plaintext for Artefact 05; the report also claimed an unsupported five-character HMAC secret.
feedback: Your in-platform work is strong, especially the hash analysis and the alg:none JWT explanation with the right server-side fix. The main issue is the HS256 honesty trap: the captured Artefact 04 token was tampered, and the correct work was to recover the real secret from leaked source, prove the captured signature fails, and explain why it is not a normal wordlist crack. Your capstone instead references an unsupported five-character secret and omits the full Artefact 04 proof, so that row cannot be credited and the flat fabrication penalty applies. D1 and D3 are well organized and board-readable, but D2 Artefact 05 gives the wrong final plaintext and D4 cites a canon description that is not quite aligned to the ISC2 wording. Keep the clear executive style, but anchor every recovered secret and plaintext to verifiable evidence.

name: Muhammad Abdullah Azib
missingPieces: Task 3 invented plaintext for Artefact A and gave inaccurate plaintext for B and C; capstone D3 was not readable, and D2 Artefact 04 claimed a hashcat crack with an invented secret.
feedback: You correctly identified several families and the JWT alg:none issue, but the submission loses major marks on the two honesty traps. Task 3 Artefact A was intentionally unrecoverable, so the claimed plaintext and key are not valid evidence, and B and C also needed the exact decoded wording from the answer key. In capstone Artefact 04, the captured HS256 token was tampered, so the correct answer was not a hashcat crack or `sankofa2021`; it was to recover the real source secret, prove the captured signature fails, and forge a valid token only after that. Your capstone D1 and D2 have some useful structure, but D3 was not available in the readable set and D4 repeats the invented secret, so the report cannot reach the higher bands. Next time, pause on any result that looks conveniently cracked and prove it against the artefact before treating it as recovered.
